items.title: Earl May interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 11, 2001
items.q: Charles McPherson and I talk about this quite a bit.

ctx.x: In retrospect, when you think about playing with Coltrane and Miles and Charlie Parker, is there things that stick out in you mind that maybe at the time didn’t make an impression on you but in later years? That’s an awful big question.

It is. Let’s see if I can break it down. I hope I can answer your question. You know when you’re going through these things, let’s say, what I get from your question is when you’re going through these things it’s not like another gig because I was scared to death. I was really scared. But when you look back now, or even I can really see the magnitude, if there is such a word, of what I had done, you know being in those bands and playing with those great, great people. I mean if I could have done that now, I just…
